title: Teufelsberg Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Teufelsberg is a man-made hill, not a natural one.** After the Second World War, Berlin dumped its bombed rubble here for over twenty years, building an artificial hill of roughly 26 million cubic metres of debris that now rises about 120 m in the Grunewald forest, out in the west of the city.

**Under the rubble is a buried, unfinished Nazi building.** The shell of a military-technical college designed by Albert Speer sits at the base. It was so solidly built that the Allies could not easily blow it up, so they buried it under the wartime rubble instead.

**On top is a Cold War spy station.** The United States built one of its biggest listening posts here, and the white radar domes you see today are its empty shells. It was abandoned after 1990 and is now one of Europe's largest open-air street-art sites, with a 360-degree viewing platform over Berlin.

**Practical basics for 2026: open daily from 11:00 until sunset, closing earlier in winter.** Tickets are **€12 for adults, €10 reduced, €5 for under-18s and free for under-7s**. You can buy online in advance or pay at the entrance by cash or card. Last entry is one hour before closing.

**Getting there is a real trip, so plan a half day.** Take the S-Bahn to Grunewald, then walk about 2 km (30 minutes) uphill through the forest. There is free parking at the bottom. It is far from the historic centre, so I treat it as a separate Cold War day out, not a quick add-on.
